requirements: Track inventory items with a name, quantity and unit price.
Add new items or increase quantity of existing items.
Remove stock from an item, error if insufficient quantity.
Report items whose quantity is below a user‑provided threshold.
Calculate total monetary value of all stock (quantity × price).
Persist inventory data in a JSON file between runs.
Invalid input (negative numbers, missing items, malformed file) raises a clear InventoryError.
The program never crashes; all errors are caught and reported to the user.

modules.name: inventory_core
modules.purpose: Define shared exception and type alias used by all other modules.

modules.name: inventory_io
modules.purpose: Load inventory from and save inventory to a JSON file.
api: def load_inventory(path: str) -> dict[str, dict]  # reads JSON, returns inventory dict, raises InventoryError on I/O or format problems
def save_inventory(path: str, inventory: dict[str, dict]) -> None  # writes inventory as JSON, raises InventoryError on failure

modules.name: inventory_ops
modules.purpose: Perform inventory modifications and generate reports.
api: def add_item(inventory: dict[str, dict], name: str, quantity: int, price: float) -> dict[str, dict]  # adds or updates an item, raises InventoryError for non‑positive quantity/price
def remove_item(inventory: dict[str, dict], name: str, quantity: int) -> dict[str, dict]  # subtracts quantity, removes entry if zero, raises InventoryError if item missing or not enough stock
def total_value(inventory: dict[str, dict]) -> float  # sum of quantity * price for all items
def low_stock(inventory: dict[str, dict], threshold: int) -> list[dict]  # list of items with quantity < threshold; each dict has keys name, quantity, price

modules.name: app
modules.purpose: Command‑line interface that ties together I/O and operations.
api: def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int  # parses arguments, calls inventory_io and inventory_ops, prints user‑friendly messages, returns exit status

data_formats: inventory = dict[str, {'quantity': int, 'price': float}]  # mapping item name to its data
